title: Debugging & Troubleshooting
description: Master debugging techniques using Robot Framework's logging capabilities, error analysis, and timing measurement to efficiently troubleshoot test failures and performance issues.
learningObjectives: Use log levels (TRACE, DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR) to control diagnostic output visibility
Inspect all variables in scope using Log Variables for comprehensive debugging
Log multiple related values efficiently with Log Many
Write informative custom error messages for faster failure analysis
Measure and analyze keyword execution time to identify performance bottlenecks
Apply debugging best practices to reduce troubleshooting time

keyTakeaways: Log levels form a hierarchy: TRACE < DEBUG < INFO < WARN < ERROR
Use --loglevel option to control what appears in console output
Log Variables shows all variables (user-created, automatic, and library variables)
Log Many creates a single log entry with multiple values on separate lines
Custom error messages (msg= parameter) make failures easier to diagnose
Robot Framework automatically tracks execution time for all keywords and tests
Sleep keyword simulates delays but use explicit waits in real tests
log.html contains detailed timing data next to every keyword execution
Effective debugging combines appropriate log levels, variable inspection, and timing analysis
commonPitfalls: Using Sleep instead of Wait Until... keywords for synchronization
Logging sensitive data (passwords, API keys) in plain text
Excessive DEBUG/TRACE logging in production environments
Not including actual and expected values in custom error messages
Ignoring execution time data when tests become slow
Using Log Many in tight loops causing performance issues
Setting unrealistic timeouts (too short causes flakiness, too long wastes time)

realWorldApplications.description: Use log levels to create verbose logs during test failures while keeping successful runs concise
Log Variables to inspect complex API responses and diagnose data parsing issues
Monitor execution times across releases to catch performance degradation early
Use Log Many and custom error messages to capture state when intermittent failures occur
Set log level to WARN or ERROR in production to highlight only critical issues
